items.headline: Ex-policeman Kelvin Chelvam loses appeal in the fatal abuse of maid Piang Ngaih Don
items.summary: Former police officer Kelvin Chelvam, 47 — jailed 10 years for abetting the fatal abuse of Myanmar domestic worker Piang Ngaih Don — lost his appeal and was ordered to begin serving his sentence on 7 August after a one-week deferment.

items.headline: About 1.5 million Singaporeans to receive up to S$850 in GST Voucher cash this month
items.summary: Roughly 1.5 million adult Singaporeans will receive up to S$850 in GST Voucher cash in August, while about 710,000 seniors get up to S$450 in MediSave top-ups, with payouts scaled to income and home annual value.

items.headline: Man jailed 21 years and given 16 strokes for the prolonged abuse of his teenage niece
items.summary: A 38-year-old man was sentenced to 21 years' jail and 16 strokes of the cane after pleading guilty to six charges, including statutory rape, over years of sexual abuse of his niece; a further 17 charges were taken into consideration.

items.headline: Woman jailed two weeks over a knife-and-bite fight at a Geylang massage parlour
items.summary: A 40-year-old woman was jailed two weeks after she threatened a colleague with a fruit knife, which cut the victim, and bit her arm during a fight at a Geylang Road massage parlour; she was convicted under the Protection from Harassment Act and for causing hurt.

items.headline: India coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: The primary Indian outlets (The Hindu, The Indian Express, Hindustan Times, The Times of India, NDTV and The Economic Times) and the reachable international fallbacks could not be fetched from today's network environment after repeated attempts, so no India-domestic story could be verified against an allowed source with a working deep link. Regular coverage resumes tomorrow.

items.headline: UK coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: BBC and Sky News, and the fallback outlets (The Guardian, CNN, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg and CNBC), could not be reached for a verifiable UK-domestic deep link from today's network environment after repeated attempts. Regular coverage resumes tomorrow.

items.headline: Update: Trump says US-Iran talks will begin Monday after calling off a 'massive' strike
items.summary: President Trump said negotiations to end the Iran war would start Monday afternoon after he held off on what he called the biggest strike 'since World War II', aiming to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's foreign-ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said Tehran had 'no plan' for direct talks and was engaging only with Oman.

items.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's Engels bomber base and Saratov refinery; at least eight killed
items.summary: Ukraine launched one of the war's largest overnight drone raids on 2 August, igniting fires at the Engels strategic-aviation air base and the Rosneft Saratov oil refinery; Russia said it downed 635 drones. Regional governors reported at least eight people killed, including three struck in a car in Udmurtia, some 1,300km from the front.

items.headline: Update: Israeli strikes kill about 19 in Gaza, the deadliest day in weeks, despite Trump's plan
items.summary: Israeli forces killed at least 19 Palestinians across Gaza City, Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis on 2 August — the highest daily toll in weeks — days after Trump promoted a Hamas disarmament plan he called a 'monumental step'. An Israeli minister said no deal existed to halt the attacks.

items.headline: AI-deployment startup June emerges from stealth with a $20 million pre-seed
items.summary: June, founded by former Salesforce executive Efrat Rapoport and three Bonobo AI co-founders, launched on 3 August with a $20 million pre-seed led by Marc Benioff's Time Ventures, and backed by Michael Dell, Aaron Levie and George Kurtz, to make AI tools run reliably inside legacy enterprise systems.

items.headline: South Korean AI-chip designer DeepX's valuation surges to about $2.2 billion
items.summary: DeepX raised fresh Series D funding at roughly 3.14 trillion won ($2.2 billion), about four times its previous valuation, signing a first tranche of 42 billion won from existing backers BNW Investment and DS Asset Management.

items.headline: Alibaba releases a new Qwen model it says rivals leading US AI labs
items.summary: Alibaba unveiled a new frontier model, Qwen3.8-Max, on 3 August, claiming benchmark results comparable to top Western systems — the latest in a run of Chinese model launches narrowing the gap with US developers.

items.headline: Citadel Securities sees a $500 billion chip-financing debt binge by 2028
items.summary: Citadel Securities projected more than $500 billion of additional public- and private-market debt by 2028 to fund the chips inside AI data centres, underscoring how much leverage is building behind the AI buildout.

items.headline: Wall Street rallies as oil slides on Iran talks and Amazon tops $3 trillion
items.summary: US stocks jumped on 3 August — the Nasdaq Composite up about 2.3% and the Dow more than 600 points intraday — as Amazon rose past a $3 trillion market value, while WTI crude fell roughly 6% below $80 a barrel after Trump called off a strike on Iran.

items.headline: Palantir's revenue jumps 93% and it lifts its full-year guidance again
items.summary: Palantir reported second-quarter revenue up 92.8% year on year to $1.94 billion, with US commercial revenue soaring 149% to $764 million, and raised its 2026 revenue forecast to about $8.15 billion.

items.headline: Snap shares jump about 12% on a second-quarter beat and upbeat forecast
items.summary: Snap reported quarterly revenue of roughly $1.6 billion, above the $1.54 billion expected, and issued current-quarter guidance ahead of estimates, sending the stock up about 12%.

items.headline: Curium to buy radiopharma rival Lantheus in a deal worth up to $8 billion
items.summary: Radiopharmaceutical group Curium agreed to acquire Lantheus for $102.50 a share in cash plus up to $12.00 a share in milestone payments — up to $8 billion in all, a 38% premium — in a push across cancer, neurology and cardiology imaging; the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

items.headline: US copper imports hit a record as traders front-run a possible Trump tariff
items.summary: More than 200,000 metric tons of copper poured into the United States in July, the biggest monthly inflow on record since at least 2014, as traders raced ahead of a potential refined-metal tariff; combined Comex and LME inventories now exceed 740,000 tons.

items.headline: Welsh Fire end Southern Brave's unbeaten run in The Hundred
items.summary: Welsh Fire Women beat Southern Brave Women in a low-scoring match at Sophia Gardens, Cardiff, on 3 August, with Heather Graham unbeaten on 35 as they ended the Brave's perfect start and climbed to fourth in the table.

items.headline: Welsh Fire chase down Southern Brave to complete a Cardiff double
items.summary: In the men's match at Cardiff, Welsh Fire held Southern Brave to 115 for 8 and chased 116 for the loss of four wickets with five balls to spare, winning by six wickets.

items.headline: Astronomers report the first sign of an atmosphere on a rocky habitable-zone planet
items.summary: Researchers detected helium escaping from LHS 1140 b, a rocky super-Earth about 48 light-years away orbiting in its star's habitable zone — reported as the first atmosphere on a rocky world in a habitable zone, though some caution the evidence is not yet definitive.

items.headline: NASA fuels the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope for a late-August launch
items.summary: NASA loaded 290 gallons of hydrazine into the Roman Space Telescope at Kennedy Space Center, keeping it on track for a 30 August launch on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy — roughly nine months ahead of schedule.

items.headline: NASA's Psyche probe returns data and a time-lapse from its Mars flyby
items.summary: NASA released the science haul from Psyche's Mars gravity assist, when the spacecraft passed within about 2,860 miles of the planet, tested its instruments and imaged the moons Phobos and Deimos on its way to the metal-rich asteroid Psyche, due in 2029.

items.headline: A total solar eclipse will cross Iceland and northern Spain on 12 August
items.summary: On 12 August a total solar eclipse — the first over mainland Europe since 1999 — will sweep across eastern Greenland, western Iceland and northern Spain, with up to two minutes and 18 seconds of totality; ESA is running observation campaigns.

fun_fact.headline: The Netherlands is the world's second-largest food exporter
fun_fact.body: Despite being roughly the size of a small US state, the Netherlands is the world's second-largest exporter of agricultural products by value, behind only the United States, shipping well over EUR100 billion of food and plants a year. It manages this through extraordinarily intensive, high-tech farming — vast climate-controlled greenhouses and precision growing that turn a tiny, low-lying country into a global food powerhouse.
fun_fact.source: Wageningen University & Research / CBS Statistics Netherlands

puzzle.title: The Pivot Square
puzzle.body: Two identical square tiles are each 6 cm on a side. Place the second tile so that one of its corners sits exactly on the centre of the first tile, then spin the second tile around that fixed corner to any angle. As it turns, the overlap region keeps changing shape. What is the area of that overlap?
puzzle.approach: Use the square's four-fold symmetry rather than computing a changing shape.
puzzle.answer: Always 9 cm^2 — one quarter of a tile — regardless of angle. The moving tile's two edges meet at the pinned corner at 90 degrees; by the bottom tile's four-fold rotational symmetry about its centre, any 90-degree wedge from the centre and its three quarter-turn copies cover the tile exactly once, so each wedge is one quarter of the area. The moving tile's 6 cm edges always reach past the boundary (farthest boundary point is ~4.24 cm from the centre), so the overlap equals that quarter wedge: 6 x 6 / 4 = 9 cm^2.

word_puzzle.title: Sleight of Letters
word_puzzle.body: Rearrange all the letters of each phrase to form the answer. 1) THE CLASSROOM -> the person who runs it (one word, 12 letters). 2) A DECIMAL POINT -> a phrase describing what it is (4 words). 3) DORMITORY -> what an untidy one is (two words).
word_puzzle.approach: Each line uses every letter exactly once; rearrange into the target.
word_puzzle.answer: 1) THE CLASSROOM = SCHOOLMASTER. 2) A DECIMAL POINT = I'M A DOT IN PLACE. 3) DORMITORY = DIRTY ROOM. Each pair is a perfect anagram using exactly the same letters.
